key_insight: Eigenvalue-based neural constitutive models jointly learn flexible yield surfaces and evolution laws while enforcing isotropy, convexity, and thermodynamic consistency.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports data-driven modeling of rate-independent isotropic elastoplastic materials, including non-associative flow, within finite element simulations.
method: Use permutation-invariant spectral representations to enforce isotropy and convexity across learnable components.
Represent non-associative yielding by extending a convex flow potential with a jointly learned additive term.
Train through a backward-Euler return map using implicit differentiation with eigenvalue-degeneracy-aware handling.
evidence_signal: Evaluation includes reproducing known constitutive models, learning from full-field finite element stress–strain data and homogenized foam responses, and solving plane-stress boundary-value problems.
watch_item: Implementation requires robust implicit return mapping and careful differentiation near repeated eigenvalues.
paper_title: Thermodynamically consistent neural constitutive models for elastoplasticity via eigen-representations
